executive_assessment.technical_summary: All available stages agree that officecli.exe is a 64-bit Windows PE/.NET apphost-style native launcher that enters standard CRT startup and hands off through hostfxr/apphost logic. The strongest supported conclusion is about native startup and packing: no custom native unpacker or runtime unpacking milestone was established, and no unpacked artifact was produced. Runtime analysis directly confirmed entry, CRT, TLS gate, main, trace-writer setup, and exe_start/handoff breakpoints, but stopped shortly after managed host startup. Therefore maliciousness, benignness, family attribution, persistence, injection, credential access, exfiltration, and network behavior are not established from current evidence.
executive_assessment.highest_value_resolution: Static and dynamic evidence reconcile around a normal native .NET apphost startup path rather than a native unpacking shellcode or custom loader path.
executive_assessment.remaining_decision_point: The managed application payload behavior after hostfxr/apphost handoff remains unexamined and blocks a malware-versus-benign verdict.

finding_reviews.title: Sample identity and .NET apphost classification

original_claims.claim: officecli.exe at the supplied path hashes to 937db176b585e874aa5bff48d536bce78037665cd862b5deefe56e79977e6588.
The sample is a 64-bit PE with CLR-heavy imports and apphost startup flow consistent with a .NET application host.
The target exists at the supplied path and hashes to the report directory identifier.

evidence_chain.observation: The prepare stage records file_name officecli.exe, the supplied absolute path, and SHA256 937db176b585e874aa5bff48d536bce78037665cd862b5deefe56e79977e6588.
Architecture 64, image base 0x140000000, hash 937db176b585e874aa5bff48d536bce78037665cd862b5deefe56e79977e6588, and numerous CoreCLR-related symbols/strings were present.
main calls exe_start, and exe_start references hostfxr_main_startupinfo, hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo, and System.Private.CoreLib.dll.

finding_reviews.reasoning: The identity claim is independently present in prepare-env, static-pass1, unpack, and dynamic outputs with the same original SHA256. The .NET apphost classification is supported by native startup analysis plus hostfxr/System.Private.CoreLib references; no upstream evidence contradicts it.

confidence_change.justification: Hash identity is certain, but the combined reviewed finding includes apphost classification; 0.99 preserves a small margin for native-host interpretation limits.

limitations: This does not classify the managed application logic as benign or malicious.

finding_reviews.title: Native startup follows standard CRT/apphost/hostfxr path

original_claims.claim: The native entry path is normal CRT startup into hostfxr-based .NET bootstrapper rather than a custom self-unpacking loader.
Runtime confirms standard apphost startup path through entry, CRT, TLS gate, main, trace-writer setup, and exe_start.

evidence_chain.observation: Startup is the standard CRT trampoline into __scrt_common_main_seh.
exe_start resolves app_path, dotnet_root, and host_path, then calls hostfxr_main_startupinfo and hostfxr_main_bundle_startupinfo.
Breakpoints were installed and hit at ASLR-adjusted entry, CRT after cookie, TLS initialization gate, main, trace writer assignment, and exe_start.

finding_reviews.reasoning: Static control-flow interpretation was corroborated by dynamic breakpoint hits at the corresponding ASLR-adjusted addresses. This permits a direct report claim about the native startup path, but only up to hostfxr/apphost handoff.

confidence_change.justification: Dynamic corroboration is strong, but the run stopped shortly after handoff and did not inspect managed entry internals.

limitations: Does not prove later managed code is benign or fully observed.

finding_reviews.title: No native unpacking requirement established

original_claims.claim: No strong custom packer indicators found; static indicators favor managed runtime host over custom packer/decryptor stub.
The sample exposes normal PE structure and imports, so runtime recovery was not pursued.

evidence_chain.observation: Interesting strings include CoreCLR exception/runtime markers, diagnostics IPC messages, and System.Private.CoreLib.dll.
PE import parsing found 437 imports from 17 DLLs including KERNEL32.dll, ADVAPI32.dll, ole32.dll, USER32.dll, SHELL32.dll, and UCRT API-set DLLs.
Debugger initialized a guest copy with main module base 0x00007FF7AA020000, entry 0x00007FF7AA5E6230, size 10080256, section_count 9.

finding_reviews.reasoning: The stages consistently support 'no native unpacking requirement established' rather than 'proven unpacked/benign'. No recovered artifact exists, and no candidate OEP/handoff was produced because the milestone was assessed not needed. Managed bundle extraction may still be needed for behavior analysis, but that is separate from native unpacking.

confidence_change.justification: Static and unpack triage agree; confidence remains bounded because sustained runtime tracing and managed extraction were not performed.

limitations: Moderately high section entropy or managed bundle embedding may still conceal managed content; no 04-static-pass2 artifact exists.

finding_reviews.title: Malicious behaviors were not observed in the limited runtime window

original_claims.claim: Persistence, injection, networking, and credential access were not observed during the available isolated debugger run.

evidence_chain.observation: No domains, IP addresses, mutex names, registry keys, persistence locations, injection targets, or credential-access artifacts were observed during the debugger-controlled run.
After the startup breakpoint sequence, debug_get_state returned state stopped; subsequent module_list returned an empty module list because the debugger was no longer attached to a running debuggee.

finding_reviews.reasoning: Absence was observed only in a short debugger-controlled startup window without Procmon, packet capture, managed instrumentation, or complete process lifetime tracing. The final report may say those behaviors were not observed in that window, but must not imply they are absent overall.

confidence_change.justification: The observation window ended shortly after host startup and lacked telemetry sources needed to exclude managed-stage behavior.

limitations: No packet capture, filesystem monitor, registry monitor, or API trace artifact was collected.

finding_reviews.title: No native startup anti-analysis gate blocked execution

original_claims.claim: No failing debugger, timing, or gate-value check was encountered before hostfxr/apphost handoff.

evidence_chain.observation: debug_run advanced through the planned gate/startup breakpoints to exe_start and then into external runtime code without analyst patches to flags, branches, or gate values.

finding_reviews.reasoning: The direct evidence supports no native-startup blocking gate in the traced path. It does not rule out managed anti-analysis checks after apphost handoff or environment-dependent paths not triggered in the run.

confidence_change.justification: Scope is constrained to native startup; managed anti-analysis remains untested.

limitations: Managed-code checks after hostfxr startup were not instrumented.

contradictions.topic: Static environment readiness versus completed static analysis

claims.claim: Static environment status is blocked because /ida-pro:idapython skill was unavailable.
Static pass 1 completed IDB open and survey successfully.

contradictions.analysis: The apparent conflict is environmental, not analytical. Prepare-env checked for a specific Claude skill path, while static-pass1 later used available IDA/MCP tooling or an IDB already present in the workspace. The static-pass1 JSON is valid and internally consistent with later dynamic addresses.
contradictions.resolution: Treat prepare-env's static blocker as stale or tool-specific. Do not use it to invalidate the completed static-pass1 findings.

contradictions.topic: Imported sensitive APIs versus lack of observed malicious behavior

claims.claim: Imports include VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect, CreateProcessW, GetProcAddress, LoadLibraryA/W, IsDebuggerPresent, and registry/process/runtime APIs.
No persistence, injection, networking, credential access, domains, IPs, mutexes, or registry modifications were observed during the debugger-controlled run.

contradictions.analysis: Imported APIs are capability-level and in this binary are plausibly inherited from the .NET runtime/apphost and Windows hosting libraries. The dynamic run did not observe malicious use, but it was too short and narrowly instrumented to disprove managed-stage behavior.
contradictions.resolution: Report the imports only as runtime/apphost capability surface, not as executed malicious behavior. Report dynamic non-observation with the startup-window caveat.

contradictions.topic: No native unpacking required versus managed payload unexamined

claims.claim: Unpacking was not required and no unpacked artifact was recovered or recommended for pass 2.
Meaningful payload likely lives in managed assemblies or runtime-loaded content not fully visible in native apphost analysis.
Managed payload behavior remains the primary unknown after native startup tracing.

contradictions.analysis: These are not mutually exclusive when scoped carefully. Native unpacking was not indicated, but bundle/managed assembly extraction is a different analysis need. The missing 04-static-pass2 is explained by no recovered native artifact, not by completion of managed-code review.
contradictions.resolution: Allow 'no native unpacking requirement established'; prohibit 'payload fully analyzed' or 'benign' conclusions until managed payload inspection occurs.

hypotheses.statement: Any security-relevant behavior, if present, is more likely in the bundled managed officecli.dll/application layer than in the native apphost startup code.
validation_plan: Extract or locate bundled managed assemblies from officecli.exe.
Analyze managed entry point and configuration for filesystem, network, persistence, process, credential, and update behavior.
Repeat dynamic run with managed instrumentation or system telemetry through full application execution.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: A complete managed-code review and full telemetry run show no additional application logic beyond standard host startup or show native code independently performs the behavior before managed entry.

hypotheses.statement: The process stopping shortly after host handoff may be due to missing runtime/application prerequisites, CLI argument requirements, normal fast exit, or debugger/run-control limitations rather than an anti-analysis block.
validation_plan: Run with expected CLI arguments and collect stdout/stderr/exit code in the isolated guest.
Collect Procmon/ETW and module-load telemetry through process termination.
Break on process exit and managed assembly load events to identify termination reason.
hypotheses.falsification_condition: A reproduced stop is directly tied to a specific anti-debug/anti-VM branch or to an observed managed exception with diagnostic output explaining termination.

allowed_claims: officecli.exe is the analyzed file and its SHA256 is 937db176b585e874aa5bff48d536bce78037665cd862b5deefe56e79977e6588.
The native binary is a 64-bit Windows PE consistent with a .NET apphost/self-contained runtime carrier.
Static and dynamic evidence confirmed the native startup path through standard CRT/apphost logic to exe_start/hostfxr handoff.
No unpacked native artifact was produced, and available evidence did not establish a custom native unpacker requirement.
caveated_claims: No persistence, injection, credential-access, network, mutex, registry, or host IOC behavior was observed during the limited debugger-controlled startup window only.

Sensitive imports such as memory, process, registry, debugger, and dynamic-loading APIs are present, but current evidence supports treating them as capability/runtime surface rather than executed malicious behavior.
No native startup anti-analysis gate was observed before hostfxr/apphost handoff; managed-stage anti-analysis remains untested.
The managed application payload likely requires separate extraction/analysis before reaching a malware or benign verdict.
prohibited_claims: Do not claim ransomware behavior, destructive impact, encryption, wipers, or data destruction.
Do not claim persistence, injection, credential theft, collection, exfiltration, command-and-control, or network communication as observed behavior.
Do not assign a malware family or campaign attribution from current evidence.
Do not claim payload execution beyond native apphost/hostfxr startup handoff.
Do not claim the sample is benign solely because native startup appears standard or because no behavior was observed in the short run.
Do not report imported APIs, strings, or runtime components as executed malicious actions without direct execution evidence.

limitations: No 04-static-pass2.json is present because no native recovered artifact was produced.
No explicitly supplied external-intelligence JSON was available for reconciliation.
Dynamic analysis was limited to x64dbg MCP startup tracing and did not include packet capture, Procmon/ETW, filesystem monitor, registry monitor, or memory dump artifacts.
Managed-code internals and application-level behavior after hostfxr/apphost handoff were not analyzed.
Prepare-env reported the specific /ida-pro:idapython skill unavailable, though later static analysis completed through available tooling.
